issues.t: Worn valve stem seals make the V8 burn oil
issues.sym: Blue-gray smoke from the exhaust at startup or after coasting, and needing to add oil between changes.
issues.why: The rubber valve stem seals on the N62 V8 harden from engine heat and let oil slip into the cylinders.
issues.next: Track how much oil the car uses. Small amounts can be lived with; heavy smoke or fouled spark plugs mean the seals need replacing, which is a big labor job.

issues.t: Plastic cooling parts crack and the engine overheats
issues.sym: Coolant leaks, a sweet smell, white crust on hose connections, the low-coolant warning, or rising engine temperature.
issues.why: The thermostat housing, radiator end tanks, water pump impeller and hoses are plastic and become brittle after years of heat cycles.
issues.next: Don't keep driving if the engine overheats. If there's no record of a cooling system refresh, plan to replace the aging parts as a set.

issues.t: Valve cover and oil filter housing gaskets leak oil
issues.sym: Burning oil smell, light smoke from the engine bay, and oil on the engine or the belly pan.
issues.why: The gaskets on the valve covers and oil filter housing shrink and harden with age. On the V8 the job takes longer because of how the engine is packed in.
issues.next: Have the leak found and fixed before oil reaches the exhaust or soaks the belts and alternator.

issues.t: Automatic transmission shifts harshly or leaks fluid
issues.sym: Harsh, late or jerky shifts, delayed engagement into drive or reverse, or red fluid under the car.
issues.why: The ZF 6-speed automatic's fluid was sold as lifetime, so it often never gets changed. Worn solenoids, old fluid and a leaking plastic sleeve where the wiring enters the transmission are common causes.
issues.next: Have the fluid level checked and the codes read. A fluid and filter change, new sleeve and pan gasket, and a software update fix many cases.

issues.t: SMG gearbox pump fails on the M6
issues.sym: The car won't select a gear, gets stuck in one gear, shows a transmission warning, or won't start.
issues.why: The M6's automated manual (SMG) gearbox shifts using a hydraulic pump that wears out with age. Its clutch also wears faster than a normal manual.
issues.next: Have a BMW M specialist read the SMG codes and test the pump. Plan for clutch replacement every 60,000 to 80,000 miles depending on use.

issues.t: Rod bearing wear on the M6 V10
issues.sym: Often no sign until it's serious. Later, knocking from the engine, low oil pressure warnings, or metal in the oil.
issues.why: The high-revving S85 V10 wears its connecting rod bearings as mileage builds. A failed bearing can destroy the engine.
issues.next: Keep oil changes frequent and ask for proof of bearing service. Many M specialists replace the bearings as preventive maintenance.

issues.t: Throttle actuators fail on the M6
issues.sym: Surging, a sudden drop into limp mode, warning lights, or the car refusing to accelerate.
issues.why: The V10 uses motor-driven throttle actuators whose internal gears and circuit boards wear out.
issues.next: Have the codes read. A failed actuator is replaced and the throttle system recalibrated.

issues.t: iDrive screen freezes, reboots or goes blank
issues.sym: The center screen freezes, restarts by itself, goes black, or phones won't connect.
issues.why: Early iDrive units in particular are known for software and hardware faults; later units are better but can still lock up.
issues.next: Try a system reset and ask a dealer for the latest software. If the unit has failed, a used or later-version unit is often the fix.

issues.t: Convertible top stops or works slowly
issues.sym: The soft top moves slowly, stops partway, won't latch, or won't open or close at all.
issues.why: The top runs on a hydraulic pump and cylinders with small position switches. Pumps wear out, cylinder seals leak, and switches fail.
issues.next: Test the top several times before buying. Have a specialist read the top codes before replacing big parts; a switch or leaking cylinder is often the cause.

issues.t: Battery drains overnight
issues.sym: The car won't start after sitting, or shows battery drain warnings.
issues.why: Some modules, such as the comfort access and trunk release modules, may not go to sleep and keep drawing power.
issues.next: Have the battery tested and a parasitic drain test done. A BMW scan tool helps find which module stays awake.

issues.t: Front control arm bushings wear and the wheel shakes when braking
issues.sym: Clunks over bumps, a steering wheel shake when braking, loose steering, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: The front control arm bushings on these heavy coupes and convertibles crack and wear out with age and mileage.
issues.next: Have the front suspension checked. New arms or bushings and an alignment usually fix it.

issues.t: Engine computer can stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls and may not restart; steering and brakes get heavy.
issues.why: Some engine management control units were not built to specification.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN with a BMW dealer; the unit is replaced free.

issues.t: Static discharge can stall the V8 in cold weather (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls, usually in cold, dry weather.
issues.why: Static electricity at the fuel rails can disturb the engine computer.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have a BMW dealer confirm that the extra ground cables were installed.

issues.t: Brake vacuum pump valve can leak oil and weaken the brakes (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal gets harder to push and the car takes longer to stop.
issues.why: A check valve in the brake vacuum pump can leak oil into the brake booster over time, reducing power assist.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check your VIN with a BMW dealer to confirm the recall work was done.

issues.t: Twin-turbo V8 burns oil from worn valve stem seals
issues.sym: Blue smoke at startup or when slowing down, an oil smell, and the oil level dropping quickly.
issues.why: On the 650i's N63 V8 the turbos sit between the cylinder banks, and that heat wears out valve stem seals early.
issues.next: Check oil often. Ask whether BMW's Customer Care Package updates were done. Heavy smoking means the seals need replacing.

issues.t: Turbochargers fail on the 650i
issues.sym: Loss of power, a whining or siren noise, smoke, or oil in the intake.
issues.why: The hot-V layout cooks the turbochargers and their oil lines, so they wear out sooner than on other engines.
issues.next: Have boost and oil leaks checked at the first sign. Turbo replacement on this V8 is a big job.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump fails
issues.sym: Long cranking, rough idle, hesitation, misfires, or the engine dropping into reduced power.
issues.why: The high-pressure pump that feeds the direct-injection system wears internally.
issues.next: Have fuel pressure codes read. A failing pump is replaced; ask the dealer about any extended coverage.

issues.t: Fuel injectors fail on the 650i V8
issues.sym: Rough running, misfires, a fuel smell, or a check engine light.
issues.why: Deposits build on the injector tips, or the injectors fail electrically.
issues.next: Get misfire codes diagnosed. Injectors are often replaced in sets.

issues.t: Valve cover and oil separator leak on the 640i
issues.sym: A burning oil smell and oily residue on top of the engine.
issues.why: Heat cycles break down the valve cover gasket and the built-in crankcase vent system on the N55 engine.
issues.next: Have it repaired before oil gets on the exhaust or ignition coils.

issues.t: Thermostat and plastic coolant pipes fail on the 640i
issues.sym: The temperature gauge swings, coolant goes missing, or an overheating warning appears.
issues.why: The electric thermostat and plastic coolant pipes on the N55 are weak points.
issues.next: Stop if the engine overheats. Above about 80,000 miles many owners replace the cooling parts as a set.

issues.t: Rod bearing wear on the M6
issues.sym: Knocking at idle or under load.
issues.why: The M6's S63 V8 rod bearings can wear early, especially on cars used on track.
issues.next: Have oil analysis and a specialist inspection done. Preventive bearing replacement is common.

issues.t: Trunk seals leak and the carpet gets wet
issues.sym: Wet carpet or water in the trunk.
issues.why: The trunk seals are known to fail on this generation.
issues.next: Have the seals replaced and dry the trunk out to prevent electrical damage.

issues.t: Auxiliary water pump can overheat and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. Possibly smoke or a burning smell from the engine bay.
issues.why: The circuit board in the electric auxiliary water pump that cools the turbos can overheat.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for open recalls. Park outdoors until the pump is replaced.

issues.t: Fuel pump wiring in the tank can fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls or won't start, or there is a fuel smell.
issues.why: Crimped wire contacts on the in-tank fuel pump can loosen, melt the connector or stop the pump.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have a BMW dealer check your VIN; the fuel pump module is replaced free.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning. The problem only shows in a crash.
issues.why: A manufacturing defect can make the driver's airbag inflator rupture when it deploys, throwing metal pieces.
issues.next: Get the recall done as soon as possible; the driver airbag is replaced free.

issues.t: Seat side airbags may not deploy (recall)
issues.sym: No warning. The problem only shows in a crash.
issues.why: The igniters in the seat-mounted side airbags may not fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN with BMW; the airbag modules are replaced free.

issues.t: Rearview camera image can go missing (recall)
issues.sym: Part or all of the backup camera picture is missing when reversing.
issues.why: Camera software or settings can leave the rearview image blank or blocked.
issues.next: Have a BMW dealer update the camera software.

issues.t: Transmission control unit can leak and cut power (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden loss of drive power or a transmission warning.
issues.why: A weld seam on the transmission control unit cover can let fluid into the electronics.
issues.next: Have the recall done. Dealers replace the module and fluid as needed. NHTSA recall number: 23V-821.

issues.t: Starter can overheat and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: A starter that won't turn the engine, followed by a burning smell after repeated tries.
issues.why: If the starter fails and the driver keeps trying to start the car, the starter can overheat and ignite nearby parts.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Don't keep cranking a car that won't start. Check your VIN; dealers update software and replace the starter free.

issues.t: Driveshaft connection to the rear differential can fail (recall)
issues.sym: Loss of power to the rear wheels, or the car rolling if the parking brake isn't set.
issues.why: The connection between the driveshaft and rear differential may be damaged.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. Have a BMW dealer inspect and repair it under the recall.

issues.t: Brakes squeal when coming to a stop
issues.sym: A loud squeal when slowing from about 30 mph to a stop, even on fairly new cars. Stopping power is normal.
issues.why: Brake dust and the factory pad material are the suspected cause, especially with the M Sport brakes.
issues.next: Have the brakes checked. Many owners switch to aftermarket pads to quiet them.

issues.t: Front tires wear out fast on the edges
issues.sym: Inner or outer edges of the front tires wear down quickly, sometimes in about 10,000 miles.
issues.why: The factory alignment settings are hard on tires, especially on xDrive cars.
issues.next: Check the inner tire edges often. A specialist alignment or longer-wearing tires can help.

issues.t: Low coolant warning or coolant leaks
issues.sym: A low-coolant warning that comes and goes, or coolant drips under the car.
issues.why: New engines absorb some coolant into seals, which BMW says is normal. Plastic hoses, the expansion tank and turbo coolant lines can also leak.
issues.next: Top up with BMW coolant. If the warning keeps returning, have the system pressure-tested for leaks.

issues.t: Twin-turbo V8 burns or leaks oil on the M850i
issues.sym: Oil spots or oil in the engine bay, bluish smoke from the exhaust, or adding a quart every few thousand miles.
issues.why: The turbos sit between the cylinder heads and run very hot, wearing seals and gaskets.
issues.next: Keep track of oil use. Gasket leaks are simple to fix; valve stem seal work is a much bigger job.

issues.t: Valve cover and crankcase vent valve leak on the 3.0L six
issues.sym: Oil leaks, a burning oil smell, a whistle from the engine, rough idle, or a puff of smoke.
issues.why: The crankcase vent (PCV) valve is built into the plastic valve cover on the B58 engine, and the cover's gasket can leak.
issues.next: Have the valve cover and vent valve checked. A failed vent valve means replacing the whole valve cover.
